raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`enable_batch_invariant_mode()` replaces `torch.bmm` with `bmm_batch_invariant`, but the `set_batch_invariant_mode()` context manager only restored `_batch_invariant_MODE` and the aten library when it exited. After the first `with set_batch_invariant_mode(): ...` in a process, every later `torch.bmm` call kept going through the batch-invariant Triton kernel.

A caller that runs after the context (for example a test computing an fp32 reference with `torch.bmm`) then silently uses a different kernel than it expects and gets different numerics, and the outcome depends on which code ran earlier in the same process.

## Modifications

- `set_batch_invariant_mode()` saves `_original_torch_bmm` and `torch.bmm` together with the mode and library on entry, and restores all of them on exit.
- The restore moved into a `finally` block, so an exception raised inside the context also leaves `torch.bmm` as it was found.

Behaviour inside the context is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

Checked directly on a GPU host:

```python
import torch
from sglang.srt.batch_invariant_ops import set_batch_invariant_mode

bmm = torch.bmm
with set_batch_invariant_mode():
    assert torch.bmm is not bmm          # replaced inside
assert torch.bmm is bmm                  # restored on exit (fails before this change)
try:
    with set_batch_invariant_mode():
        raise RuntimeError("boom")
except RuntimeError:
    pass
assert torch.bmm is bmm                  # restored after an exception too
```

Before this change the second assertion fails: `torch.bmm` is still `bmm_batch_invariant` after the context exits. The existing `test/registered/unit/batch_invariant_ops/test_batch_invariant_ops.py` calls `torch.bmm` only inside the context, so its expectations are unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed, according to [Writing Documentation](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#writing-documentation).
- [ ] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed, according to [Benchmark and Profiling](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/benchmark_and_profiling.html) and [Accuracy Results](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#accuracy-results).
- [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging the PR.
- [ ] Please feel free to join our Slack channel at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss your PR.

detail.title: [Fix] batch-invariant: restore torch.bmm when set_batch_invariant_mode exits

files.patch:
@@ -1240,16 +1240,30 @@ def disable_batch_invariant_mode():
 
 @contextlib.contextmanager
 def set_batch_invariant_mode(enabled: bool = True):
-    global _batch_invariant_MODE, _batch_invariant_LIB
-    old_data = (_batch_invariant_MODE, _batch_invariant_LIB)
+    global _batch_invariant_MODE, _batch_invariant_LIB, _original_torch_bmm
+    # enable_batch_invariant_mode() also replaces torch.bmm; restore it on exit,
+    # or every later torch.bmm in the process stays batch-invariant.
+    old_data = (
+        _batch_invariant_MODE,
+        _batch_invariant_LIB,
+        _original_torch_bmm,
+        torch.bmm,
+    )
     if enabled:
         enable_batch_invariant_mode()
     else:
         disable_batch_invariant_mode()
-    yield
-    if _batch_invariant_LIB is not None:
-        _batch_invariant_LIB._destroy()
-    _batch_invariant_MODE, _batch_invariant_LIB = old_data
+    try:
+        yield
+    finally:
+        if _batch_invariant_LIB is not None:
+            _batch_invariant_LIB._destroy()
+        (
+            _batch_invariant_MODE,
+            _batch_invariant_LIB,
+            _original_torch_bmm,
+            torch.bmm,
+        ) = old_data
 
 
 AttentionBlockSize = namedtuple("AttentionBlockSize", ["block_m", "block_n"])
